newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries off to sluggish start pre-FOMC, NAPM.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries off to sluggish start pre-FOMC, NAPM.

text.p: Treasuries opened a touch lower before the release of the National Association of Purchasing Management report and the afternoon start of the two-day Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

After surprisingly strong reports from regional purchasers jolted the market on Monday, the June NAPM report should overshadow construction spending data and leading economic indicators from May, all due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
"There is a little bit of nervousness ahead of that number," said Matt Alexy, chief market strategist at Credit Suisse First Boston.
"NAPM really is the issue for today. Construction spending is a little bit more of an afterthought," he added.
The T-bond opened down 2/32 at 97-28/32 with a yield of 6.79 percent. The 10-year note was also off 2/32 at 100-26/32, yielding 6.51 percent.
Economists polled by Reuters were unanimous in expecting no change in rates from the Fed at this meeting, which gets rolling at 1430 EDT/1830 GMT.
Experts said the market will nonetheless be on guard, especially on Wednesday, when the meeting concludes.
"That is when they put together the tone for the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, so it will be very important," Alexy said.

"The problem is we're not going to hear much about it until (July 22) and very few presidents or governers are going to want to put themselves in the position where they preempt Chairman (Alan) Greenspan." he said.
The NAPM index is the first real snapshot of the overall economy in June and is expected to come in at 56.4, off from 57.1 in May.

Construction spending is expected to have risen 0.5 percent in May, after a 1.0 percent fall in April, while May leading indicators are seen 0.2 percent higher, on the heels of a 0.1 percent decline previously.
Barring a big surprise from NAPM, the markets are expected to cautiously look past today's data towards Thursday's key report on June non-farm payrolls.

"I still see a sideways trading pattern until employment," said Roseanne Briggen, bond analyst at MCM MoneyWatch. "We're not going to see any major moves unless NAPM has strong numbers built into it."
Treasuries showed little reaction the BTM/Schroders report on Tuesday showing a 0.1 percent rise in chain store sales in the week ended June 28.
In other trade, the five-year note was off 2/32 at 99-12/32, yielding 6.40 percent.
In the bill sector, threes were flat at 5.12 percent and sixes were up one basis point at 5.14 percent in morning trade.
